How khyzr sounds and how its copy is written. The personality, the eight rules, how a sentence lands, the mechanics, the words, and the name.

Approachable. Transparent. Dependable. The brand looks enterprise-formal; the person you meet in the writing is human. First person "we", direct "you". No exclamation marks, no hype adjectives, no emoji, ever. The three words, glossed Approachable. We write the way we talk across a table. Transparent. We say what we see, and what we don't know yet. Dependable. We promise only what we will do. Then we do it.

Approachable, transparent, dependable, in every sentence. Talk like a human. Plain, conversational sentences. No copywriter punctuation: no em-dash constructions, no colon-heavy headlines. Empathetic, never accusatory. The buyer's past choices were reasonable. Concrete over metaphor. Say what actually happens: "the work comes back in separate pieces from separate teams," not "silos." Calm and assured, never scrappy or underdog. khyzr has reach; write like it. Forward-motion language. The brand moves things; sentences should too. Never frame the relationship as ending. No "when we're done," no "we leave you with." Permanence is earned, not declared, so we never declare it either; we just never write the goodbye. Candor as integrity. We tell you what we see, not what you want to hear. Why each rule holds 1 These three words are who we are. A sentence that shows none of them could be anyone's. 2 We look formal on purpose. The writing is where you meet the person. 3 Hiring a big name was the reasonable move. We say so, and start from there. 4 Our category speaks in big nouns. We make concrete promises instead. 5 The reader has a lot at stake. They should feel covered, not sold to. 6 What a client should remember is a business moving forward. A sentence that sits still argues against it. 7 Work has phases. The relationship stays open. 8 Integrity is the root. Candor is how it sounds.

The signature moves. The turn. The sentence ends on a reversal: "…what we see, not what you want to hear." One turn per paragraph, at most. The callback. One phrase may recur per page, as an echo, not a chorus. The reassure. Where an action asks for someone's time, one line beneath it lowers the stakes: "A short conversation to see if we're the right fit." Ask, then soften. Long–short rhythm. A flowing sentence, then a clipped one: "It's never just one thing." The short sentence carries the weight. Two-beat headlines. Period-terminated pairs: "Every discipline. One team." · "Strive Forward. Thrive Together." The second beat gets the green word.

He gave counsel, and the credit stayed with the people he helped. One name moment per surface: the Arabic name appears once, and only in that moment, set in Noto Naskh Arabic. How the names are written Lowercase holds at the start of a sentence and in a headline. Today that is two products: khyzr.ai and khyzr.studio. A product's name is written as it is addressed: lowercase, one dot, no space. Never "khyzr AI", never "Khyzr.ai", never "khyzr Studio". It settles what the record left mixed. Spelling Three sites and every document should read as one company, so we spell one way. American English: color, center, organization, program, license, gray, traveled, and the -ize endings. The serial comma, always: "growth, health, and wealth." Al-Khidr takes its hyphen. Another company's name, product, or headline keeps its own spelling: Amazon Bedrock, not "AWS Bedrock". Punctuation The rules ban the copywriter's dash, and a rule with exceptions gets argued, so we use none. No em dash anywhere. A period, a comma, or a colon does its work. An en dash only for a range in a table or a label: 11–13px. In a sentence, write "to". No exclamation marks, no emoji, no ellipses. Middle dots (·) join taxonomy labels: "Finance · Accounting". Double quotation marks, single inside them. "and" in a sentence. "&" only in a label or in a name that owns one: Sales & Marketing. Numerals Numbers are proof, so they should be easy to read and hard to misread. One to nine in words. 10 and up in figures. Always figures with a unit, in money, in percentages, in sizes, and in data: 3%, $3,900, 24px, a 30-minute call. A number never starts a sentence as a figure. Write the word, or turn the sentence. Thousands take a comma: 1,020. The percent sign and the unit sit closed up: 12%, 24px. A leading zero belongs to the numerals of a numbered list, in the technical face: 01, 02. Never in a sentence. A proof number is set large, with its unit beside it and a caption in the technical face. Dates and times A date should read one way to everyone, wherever they are. Day, month, year, the month in words: 5 October 2026. No "th", no commas. In a table, the short month: 5 Oct 2026. Never all figures, since 5/10 and 10/5 read two ways. Month and year alone where the day adds nothing: October 2026. Brand files carry no date and no version, in their names or on their pages. A letter, a proposal, and a contract are dated, because they are records. Times on the 12-hour clock: 9:30 am. Name the time zone when readers are in more than one. Titles and headings Sentence case reads like a person. Title case reads like a form. Sentence case everywhere, headlines included. That covers slide titles, document titles, and buttons. Uppercase belongs to small labels only. A headline ends with a period. A card title, a table head, a label, a button, and a menu entry do not

The marks of khyzr and how to place them. The name leads. The symbol stands alone only where the name cannot fit.

The wordmark is khyzr's signature. It is the default mark on every page, slide, and screen. It comes in two cuts: one for white and light grounds, one for dark grounds. A mark is placed from its file. It is never redrawn, retyped, or recolored. The glowing green dot is an accent motif, not a brand mark.

s: The symbol, where the name cannot fit.
x: The symbol stands alone only in tight squares: a favicon, an avatar, an app tile, a closing mark. It holds from 24px up. Below that, the badge carries it. The symbol is never shown in one color. Its greens are the mark.

Symbol and name together, for generous room: a cover, a title slide, a letterhead, a sign. The horizontal lockup sets them side by side. The vertical lockup is for square and tall formats. Never compose symbol and name by hand. New lockups are cut from the masters only, on request.

s: The badge, for the smallest sizes.
x: Under 24px the symbol appears only on a plate: a favicon, an avatar, an app tile. The default plate is the deep green. On black or near-black surroundings the plate is white. For an avatar the badge fills the square, edge to edge, and the platform rounds it. Never the bare symbol. The badge is the full-color mark on its plate. It is not a one-color mark.

Where color cannot print or render, the wordmark goes to black or white. Engraving, embossing, foil, single-color print. The black wordmark goes on light grounds, and the white one on dark grounds. There is no one-color symbol, and none will be cut. The black is a soft black and the white an off-white. Both come with the file.

Clear space is one blade of the symbol, on every side. A blade is one of the symbol's four small arcs. Nothing enters that room: no type, no edge, no other mark. Around the wordmark alone there is no blade to measure, so the room is the height of its z. In a lockup, measure the blade of its own symbol. A file is cut to its ink. No clear space is built in, so leave it yourself.

Each mark has a floor, once for screens and once for print. Wordmark 90px wide 20 mm wide Symbol 24px 8 mm Badge 16px 6 mm Horizontal lockup 120px wide 30 mm wide Vertical lockup 120px wide 20 mm wide Below a mark's floor, use the next mark down: the wordmark, then the symbol, then the badge. Engraving, embroidery, foil, and screen print take the one-color wordmark at 30 mm wide or more. The floors for the ® set and the product marks are on the brand site, under [Logo files](../logo-files/#never-smaller-than-this).

The mark holds the left edge. One khyzr mark to a surface is enough. A page. Top left, in the header. A cover with a picture carries it bottom left, on the white under the picture. A slide. Bottom left on every working slide, and on the cover, on the white under the picture. On the closing slide, top left. A screen. Top left, the wordmark alone. A lockup may sit centered on a cover or a card. The wordmark alone stays left. The tagline is set as type, apart from the mark. There is no tagline lockup.

Eight ways to break the mark, each as wrong as the last. Don't stretch or squeeze it. Don't recolor it or tint it. Don't set the symbol in one color. Don't build your own lockup. Don't add a shadow, an outline, or a glow. Don't tilt it or turn it. Don't set it on the gradient's greens, or straight on a photograph. Don't crowd it.

Ink and white lead. One green carries the brand, and it is rare. Four secondaries each have one job.

A khyzr surface is mostly white, with ink for the type. Green arrives last and small, so that it is always the point. A working ratio, not law: white 45 · ink 40 · green 10 · everything else 5. On a white page, green is the last words of a title, a dot, a rule. About one part in fifty. A piece may end dark: Ink or Pitch for the last page or slide, with white type and one light green accent.

khyzr Green is the brand's color, and the name's meaning. Its family runs deeper and lighter around it, and each member has a place. khyzr Green is the accent: the green phrase in a title, a rule, a dot, the first series of a chart. Forest and Deep Forest are the dark fields and deep fills. The deep green is darker still: the plate behind the badge, a dark panel, the dark end of the gradient. Mint and Pale Mint are the light: a pale panel, a dot, type on a dark field. Light green is the accent on a dark ground, where khyzr Green would sink: the green phrase in a white title. One green family carries the brand. Photographs are never tinted green.

Paper is white. Ink is the black that sets every title. Between them sit the grays for reading text, captions, and hairlines. Titles are Ink. Reading text is Body, a softer gray-black. Supporting text is Muted, a mid gray. Light gray sets a section apart from the white around it. Hairline draws the rules and the borders. Pitch is the darkest ground. It is never a text color.

Screens show khyzr's deep greens brighter than process ink can print them. Plan for it. khyzr Green, Forest, Deep Forest, and the deep green print a little duller and yellower than they look on screen. One family does the work. Outfit sets every title, sentence, and button. Three other faces each have one small job.

Outfit is khyzr's typeface: geometric, tight, calm. It sets everything a person reads at length or at a glance. Outfit. Titles, statements, reading text, buttons, captions. Three weights, by role. Manrope. Small labels only: uppercase, widely tracked, never a sentence. Instrument Serif. One italic aside, lowercase, at most once on a page. The rarest of the four: none of the three sites uses it. Noto Naskh Arabic. The name, الخضر, in its one moment. Nowhere else. There is no monospace.

Weight is set by the job a line does, never by eye. Semibold for titles, numbers, and quotes. Medium for names inside cards and lists, and for buttons. Regular for reading. Emphasis inside reading text is semibold, never italic.

A khyzr headline is a sentence in ink: tight, left aligned, sentence case, ending with a period. One green phrase, at most. The payoff, usually the last words. In "Every discipline. One team.", the green falls on "One team." Tight up top, open below. Large type tracks tight, and tighter as it grows. Labels track wide. Reading text stays neutral. Small beside large. Supporting text is small and gray, on a short line, about a third the size of its title. It never competes. Uppercase belongs to the labels only.

The one place khyzr uses uppercase. A label names a thing: a caption under a number, a column head, a page's folio. Manrope, semibold, uppercase, widely tracked. Small, and never smaller than 11px on a screen. Never a sentence, and never a headline. khyzr.ai and khyzr.studio set their labels in Outfit and use no Manrope.

s: Black leads. Ember is an event.
x: A khyzr.studio surface is black, with Bone and Ash for the words. Ember arrives when something responds, arrives, or is chosen. Once in a piece, it takes a whole surface. A working ratio, not law: black 65 · warm near-black 12 · bone and ash 5 · the work's own colors 5 · ember 12. Nearly all of that ember is one surface. Outside it, ember is about two parts in a hundred. One ember surface to a piece: one slide in a deck, one band on a page, one post in a set of three. At rest, a surface is black, Bone, Ash, and hairlines. The work that is shown keeps its own colors. Ember never tints it. The black is true black, not a dark gray and not a dark brown.

Ember is an even staircase of five, each step a little darker and a little redder than the last. Ember 1 Yellow The brand color. The .studio of the name, and every flat accent: a rule, an underline, a tick, a tag Ember 2 Amber The warm middle of a gradient. The lit edge of the lacquer form Ember 3 Orange The hot stop. The base of the ember field. The .studio on white Ember 4 Coral The deep foot of the ember field. Where a moving light begins Ember 5 Rose The last step. Never small text Ember is a state, not a text color. Words are Bone and Ash. The five in order are an index: five pillars of work, five steps, first to last. Never out of order, and never five for decoration. A gradient runs through neighboring steps, in the ramp's order. It never jumps a step and never leaves the ramp. The grounds and the inks Black is the page, the slide, and the ground of every still. Ink 1 and Ink 2 are the first and second steps up from black: a plate, a band, a panel one step raised. Hairline draws every rule and border. Bone is headings and the words that matter, and the product's own paper. Ash is the echo, the caption, the supporting line. The grays are warm. A neutral gray from another palette looks wrong beside them. The accent follows the ground Black Bone, with .studio in Yellow Yellow, as a line or a small mark Bone, its own paper One ink, black No ember line and no ember type. Ember only as a solid block, with black on it The ember field One ink, black, or the name typed in black None. Yellow only on a black object that stands on the field White, a page that is not its own Near-black, with .studio in Orange The .studio, and nothing more Type on ember is black. Never white, and never Bone. Yellow is for black. On Bone or white it is too pale to carry a line or a word.

One typeface, Outfit, at Semibold, Medium, and Regular. No second face, no labels in capitals, no italic. khyzr.studio speaks as khyzr does. The rules are on the [Voice](../voice/) page. These are its own habits. A head is a pair: a claim, then a quieter line that finishes the thought. Headlines are short and declarative, and end on a period. Labels are plain nouns. A step is named in one word. It speaks to "you", in short sentences. The work is named as a designer names it. The name is khyzr.studio, lowercase, wherever it stands. The one action is "Get started". American spelling.

How khyzr moves, as an idea. Things grow in. The curves and the clocks are in the design system.

khyzr's motion behaves like growth. It is called the Green Trace. An element rises crisp from its own baseline, with a breath of overshoot, and settles. Elements arrive overlapping, one while the last is still moving. Growth, not a queue. Never a flicker, never out of focus. Nothing animates twice. The idea, in three cases. Type rises from its baseline. Bars grow from theirs, and numbers count up to their value. On a screen that can run it, the mesh drifts slowly behind white type.

The Green Trace. Things grow in. Four curves, seven clocks, and the rules for everything that moves on a khyzr page.

khyzr's motion behaves like growth. An element rises crisp from its own baseline, with a breath of overshoot, and overlaps the one before it as it enters. Never a queue, never a flicker, never out of focus. It serves a line from the voice: "They say grass grew wherever he stood. We hold ourselves to that: where we work, things should be growing that weren't before."

Four rules, no exceptions. Springs move things, never colors. The overshoot curves apply to transforms only. Color, background, border, and opacity change on ease-standard. A hue cannot bounce. Entrances overlap. Grouped elements start one dur-stagger apart, while the one before is still moving. Growth, not a queue. Nothing animates twice. One arrival for each element in a page view. Coming back to a section does not replay it. Ambient loops are the only repeaters: a hero's orb, a marquee, a turning wall of quotes, the mesh's drift. Motion is a privilege. Reduced motion gets final states at once: no autoplay, and hovers keep working without transforms. No GPU means a still, never a broken simulation. Motion is a behavior of screens. Print, decks, and collateral do not animate.

The curves, plotted, and the clocks. Curves ease-trace entrances and big moves: a soft spring with a slight overshoot ease-pop hovers and pulses: a livelier overshoot for small distances ease-drift growing bars, widths, and rules, and a card's lift: decisive, with no overshoot, since a bar cannot shrink past zero ease-standard color, background, border, and opacity Clocks dur-enter an entrance dur-stagger the step between entrances, overlapping dur-hover a hover that moves: a grow, a lift, a slide dur-pulse the settle pulse dur-count a count-up dur-color a color, a border, or a ground answering the pointer dur-surface a surface changing state, such as a navigation bar turning from paper to ink Distances Rise: rise-distance. Entrance scale: from rise-scale to 1, anchored at the baseline, the element's bottom center. Card lift: 4px. Button grow: 1.05. Under a press: .98, and .95 for a round control. Arrow slide: 4px. Settle pulse: 1.07.

What does not move, eases. A change of color, background, border, or opacity runs on ease-standard, between 200 and 400ms. dur-color is the quick end: a link, a border, or a plate under the pointer. dur-surface is the slow end: a whole surface changing state. A rising block's opacity fades in beside its rise, over 800 to 900ms. A photograph develops in over 700ms once it has loaded.

The moves a page is built from. Section entrance A block rises rise-distance and scales up from rise-scale, grown from its baseline, on ease-trace over dur-enter. Crisp the whole way: no blur, no filter. Overlapping stagger When several elements enter together, each starts one dur-stagger after the last, in reading order, overlapping the one before it. Like items in a set may follow closer. Count-up and settle pulse A number counts up from zero over dur-count, easing out, then lands with a pulse to 1.07 on ease-pop over dur-pulse. Under reduced motion the final value is already in the markup. Hovers and presses A button grows to 1.05 and an arrow slides 4px, on ease-pop over dur-hover. A card comes up to the paper: it lifts 4px on ease-drift, turns from surface-2 to white, and takes shadow-lift. Under a press a pill settles to .98. A hover that moves or reveals something applies only where the pointer can hover. A press answers every pointer. An outlined pill on dark stays color-only: its border brightens, and nothing grows.

Charts obey the Green Trace. Bars grow from their baseline on ease-drift. Numbers count up over dur-count with the settle pulse. One arrival for each chart in a page view: nothing loops, and nothing animates twice.

What a page keeps when motion is off the table. Reduced motion Final states everywhere. No autoplay, no scroll easing, no drift. Hovers change color and shadow, without transforms No GPU A still of each rendered piece, at the same size No JavaScript Every block in its final place. Nothing waits to be revealed Off screen, or in a hidden tab Ambient loops stop
